reason: DB knob-tuning ML on a local DBMS is easy to run but far from OS resource management, and no repo was located so it cannot be built upon.
Application-aware NN pruning/quantization is ML-modeling work; repo exists but two case studies depend on a physical robot and a simulator that may not be reproducible.
RL query optimizer on PostgreSQL runs fine on one node but is DB query optimization, the explicitly low-scoring category for an OS course.

GPU memory profiling is on-topic for memory management and the GitHub+Zenodo artifact is single-GPU user space, though CUPTI activity APIs on a locked-down driver are a small risk and a profiler offers limited policy headroom.

Redis-compatible cache-store with thread scalability and durability is core systems work with a mature Microsoft artifact; .NET must be installed into $HOME and the codebase is large but eviction/threading knobs give real improvement space.
Batch transaction scheduling is systems-adjacent but the shared-nothing design needs colocated partitions and no repo was found.
Configurable data-transfer pipeline runs as processes on one host and has a repo, but it is data-systems plumbing rather than a resource-management problem.

Artifact-evaluated user-space hash table, but its setup script pins CPU frequency, enables explicit hugepages and disables hardware prefetchers, all requiring root/MSR that this machine cannot provide.
Single-machine C++/TBB graph pattern matching builds in user space, but it is a query engine rather than OS resource management and billion-edge LDBC data needs scale-down.
W4A8KV4 serving needs only INT4/INT8 tensor cores available on Ampere and 7-8B models fit 24 GB; repo is mature but shared with LServe and headline numbers used A100/L40S.
Compiling einsum to SQL is a query-compilation contribution with no located repo, leaving little for a systems improvement project.
Fully reproduced single-GPU superoptimizer with an active repo and clear search-heuristic headroom, but the Z3 equivalence search is expensive and kernels need retuning for sm_86.
User-space C++ range filter for LSM stores runs entirely on CPU and plugging it into RocksDB with new workloads is a clean, testable improvement axis.
Language-model NDV estimator is a learned DB statistic, close to the low-scoring learned-cardinality anchor, though ByteDance released code and it runs on one GPU.

RocksDB hot-record promotion across storage tiers is textbook OS caching/storage work on a modest 8-vCPU footprint; the promotion policy is a small tunable algorithm, only the slow tier must be emulated locally.
Poisoning robustness of learned index advisors runs on user-space PostgreSQL but is an ML-security study of a DB component, not a resource-management system.

User-space memory-tiering runtime with no kernel changes is an ideal OS topic, but the machine has one NUMA node and no PMEM/CXL so the slow tier must be emulated, changing the measurement; repo is brand new and completeness unknown.
LSM-embedded quantile sketches are a plausible user-space storage change but no artifact repo was located.
2-bit KV-cache quantization with a page-centric layout is directly KV-cache management on one GPU; released code but a very new repo, and Triton on CUDA 12.x over driver 535 is the only setup risk.
Dafny invariant inference is a formal-methods paper with no runtime resource management; the artifact installs cleanly in $HOME but improvements would be proof-coverage, not systems.

Shared-memory streaming graph engine with locality-aware updates and open competitors makes head-to-head comparison cheap on SNAP-scale graphs, but it is a graph engine rather than a core OS subsystem.
Syscall interposition is on-topic but the RDMA transport is unreachable, the container-overlay baselines need a runtime that cannot be installed, and the repo is author-marked experimental.
Single-GPU perfect hashing would run here, but no repo was located so the design cannot be built upon.

Host-offloaded training explicitly targets consumer GPUs, so 24 GB plus 125 GiB host RAM is the intended setting; the offload scheduling/prefetch policy is a clean improvement target even though the domain is 3DGS rather than a classic OS service.
Dual GPU cache with budget allocation is a genuine cache-policy problem that fits one 24 GB GPU; repo completeness and dataset scale are the open questions.
Graph-oriented LSM storage engine on a single machine is squarely a storage-engine topic with a linked repo, though the note says nothing about artifact completeness or workload availability.

CPU-only benchmark study of learned hash functions in hash tables and joins needs no special hardware and is an easy reproduce-then-extend target, but the contribution is an evaluation rather than a system.

Attention-state caching for repeated prompt segments is a caching/TTFT problem that runs on a single GPU or even CPU, with a small readable prototype and obvious admission/eviction and positional-handling extensions; accuracy control is needed for any claim.
Adapter merge/unmerge and adapter-aware batching are meaningful with a 7B base on one GPU, but the cross-replica migration half needs multiple GPUs and the artifact repo's completeness is unknown.
CPU-only lossy particle compressor would fit the machine but no repo was located.

x86-64 syscall interposition by binary rewriting matches the host ISA and is pure user space with a built-in reproduction fallback, but it may need seccomp-notify or ptrace settings this user cannot change and the repo URL came only from the paper text.
DRAM+NVMe semantic cache with slab management and eviction policies is exactly the caching topic and fits one node; only artifact completeness is unverified.
Removing regressions in learned query optimizers on PostgreSQL is cheap to run but sits in the DB query-optimizer ML category the rubric scores low.

LSM-aware replication is a real storage topic and replicas can run as processes on loopback, but every latency claim assumes a cluster and RTT-sensitive numbers would be distorted without network emulation.
User-space data/index co-compression with selective decompression fits the machine, but it is scientific-data indexing rather than an OS resource manager and artifact maturity is unknown.
Agent-skill compilation is a user-space runtime but far from OS resource management, and reproduction is bounded by LLM API cost across eight models and three harnesses.
Single-GPU TVM/Ansor tuning with a learned cost model is exactly the kind of component a course project can swap out, though it is compiler autotuning rather than a core OS subsystem.

Splitting memory between app cache and kernel page cache for RocksDB/LevelDB/WiredTiger is core OS caching, fully user space with cgroup v2 budgets plus an offline simulator, and the sizing policy is a small self-contained algorithm to improve.
Product-quantized KV-cache management for long context is directly on topic and single GPU; long-context memory pressure on 24 GB and unverified artifact completeness are the caveats.
Available+Functional Rust artifact that installs into $HOME, but half the evaluation needs RISC-V PMP hardware and the Linux runtime depends on MPK/PKU availability on this AMD CPU.
Columnar timestamp-overhead reduction is a plausible single-node storage topic but the implementation lives inside Apache IoTDB with no confirmed dedicated artifact.
Replicating SSTables instead of log entries is a genuine storage/replication co-design, but it needs several processes to emulate a cluster and no repo was located.
GPU multiplexing across PEFT tasks is a scheduling problem, but the paper targets a multi-tenant multi-GPU datacenter and Transformer Engine likely wants a newer CUDA than driver 535 supports.
Single-GPU compiler pipelining with an analytic cost model would fit, but the artifact is pinned to an older TVM/CUDA and its pipelining depths assume A100, so much of the effort becomes porting.

Predictive buffer replacement evaluated both by trace simulation and a PostgreSQL patch is a textbook cache-policy improvement target that fits this machine exactly; the linked repo is only a test-scripts repo so artifact completeness needs checking.
Package-bloat measurement is closer to a security study than resource management, and the objects of study are Docker images that would need daemonless user-space tooling to unpack here.
Warm-start matching and weight transformation are CPU-side and small models fit one GPU, but the paper's value comes from a large cluster and model zoo that must be heavily scaled down.
A benchmarking harness for GNN training systems gives a ready evaluation platform, but distributed configurations must be dropped and a measurement study leaves an ambiguous improvement target.

Trace-driven suspend/resume scheduling runs in minutes on CPU with traces shipped in the repo, but the core contribution is a competitive-ratio proof so the artifact is a numerical simulator, not a system.

Well-maintained trace schema and replay tooling with an mlsys26 branch and Zenodo archive runs on one machine, but the traces come from production clusters so any work is simulation-only and the contribution is infrastructure rather than a policy to improve.

Attention reuse that composes with paged-KV managers is close to KV-cache management and is model-agnostic single-GPU, but 128K-context evaluation needs a small model or host offload to fit 24 GB and the repo is new.

Forecast-aware autoscaling and routing is a scheduling policy studied mainly by CPU-only trace replay plus an ILP, but the real-run portion needs multi-region GPU VMs and the linked repo name (SageServe) differs from the paper.

A simulator with a documented CPU-only path needs no GPU cluster and simulator fidelity/throughput is an obvious hypothesis, but the repo is at 2.0 and may have diverged from the NSDI'25 artifact and Chakra input traces must be sourced.
3-bit MoE kernels run on Ampere but Mixtral-8x7B at 3 bits only just fits 24 GB and the contribution is mostly quantization accuracy rather than resource management.

GPU memory budgeting, PCIe transfer and SSD load balancing on a single GPU is genuinely an I/O and memory-management problem, but billion-scale corpora exceed the ~257 GB free disk and need substantial scale-down.
Incremental checkpoint/restore with dedup and CoW diffing is pure user-space state management that runs anywhere, with an active repo; only the repo-paper linkage is slightly informal.
Verus liveness proofs are a formal-methods contribution far from OS resource management, and the end-to-end controller experiments assume a Kubernetes cluster that cannot be run without Docker.

Cache revalidation policy is a clean caching topic, entirely user space with a browser plus Caddy origin, but realistic latency effects need network emulation that may want root-level tc and the repo is new.
A learned index for larger-than-memory data touches storage and buffering and needs only RAM plus local disk, but it sits in the learned-DB-component category and artifact completeness is unknown.

Client clustering is an FL algorithm rather than a systems mechanism; the FedScale simulator runs on one GPU but client populations must be scaled down and the code is a subdirectory of a large framework.
Fine-tuning a 7B model to emit DB knob configurations is ML-for-DB tuning, and even PEFT training of a Mistral-class model on 24 GB plus the DB evaluation loop is a heavy budget for the payoff.
Expert-aware pipelining for offloaded MoE inference is designed for exactly one memory-constrained GPU, but no official repo was found so the hard code-release requirement fails.

In-process monitor and custom loader build with plain make and need no root, but isolation depends on MPK whose availability on this Zen 3 part must be confirmed, and the topic is software hardening rather than resource management.
Single-node key-value store with an explicit read/write-balance tuning knob and YCSB evaluation is core storage-engine work that fits the machine, with a maintained MathWorks repo.
Offline query-plan selection is cheap to reproduce but is DB query optimization, the category the rubric scores lowest for an OS course.

A peak-memory-aware continuous-batching policy inside a serving engine on one GPU is the ideal shape for this project and the policy is easy to vary, but the code lives inside the fast-moving upstream LightLLM so locating the paper's version is extra work.

Far-memory fault/eviction balancing is a prime OS memory topic and the library-OS path is user space, but the kernel half needs root, the far-memory backend needs a second machine or RDMA, and the scalability claims target far more cores than 32 threads.
A pure multicore concurrency and memory-locality study that runs perfectly on 16 cores with a linked repo; it is an analysis paper in a DB engine context, so os_fit is adjacent rather than core.

Public code plus the AVA-100 benchmark and an LMDeploy pipeline that fits a 7-8B VLM, but the contribution is a retrieval/agent pipeline rather than systems resource management and full-benchmark indexing is compute-heavy.

A Lyapunov controller scheduling a GPU enhancement queue is scheduling-flavored with released trace-driven code, but the setting is video ABR and the strongest results come from a simulator rather than a running system.
Nested-Parquet scanning is pure user-space file-format work that would run here, but no artifact repo was located.
Tile-based video storage with a semantic index is a single-machine storage/decoding-cost problem with a repo, but it is a domain data-management system rather than a core OS subsystem.
CPU and GPU compression benchmark with a public repo runs on this machine, but the roofline analysis relies on hardware counters that are blocked and a benchmark offers a diffuse improvement target.
GNN cardinality estimation for knowledge-graph queries is the low-scoring learned-DB-estimator case and no artifact was found.

Single-GPU DNN compiler that supports sm_86 tiling, but the AE badge points at a different repository than the maintained code, which is under active refactoring, and a newer conda CUDA toolkit is likely required.

A GPU emulator built precisely so DL-systems research can run without real GPUs is an unusually good fit for this constrained machine and emulation fidelity is a natural hypothesis; artifact completeness is unverified.
Well-maintained OpenXLA repo, but GPU counter collection goes through CUPTI which is admin-restricted here and the paper's fleet-scale TPU value proposition cannot be reproduced at all.

The feature-cache and sampling-order co-design is a single-GPU-testable caching-policy question with good headroom, but the system targets multi-node multi-GPU billion-edge training and pins DGL v0.5.0 that must be built from source.
GPU JSON parsing works on one A5000 but is data-processing kernel work rather than OS resource management, and it needs a GraalVM toolchain installed in user space.

The I/O-free Rust library can run as several processes with injected partitions, but every headline result was measured on a real multi-node cluster so claims would have to be re-framed as simulation.
